title: Any nonzero explicit allowance overrides the minter infinite-allowance shortcut, so transferFrom by a minter/position reverts when the leftover allowance is smaller than the amount
description: Discovery: per-unit step 2 (conditional branch audit) and step 3 (boundary values) on allowanceInternal. The override returns the explicit allowance whenever it is > 0 and only returns INFINITY for minters/positions when the explicit allowance is exactly 0. A user holding a small leftover allowance for the MintingHub, a position or the bridge (e.g. from a prior exact-amount approve or permit) therefore gets ERC20InsufficientAllowance in transferFrom although the design intends minters to need no allowance. The user must first reset the allowance to 0 (approve(spender,0)). The state is also reachable via permit signed for a small value.
root_cause: The branch order treats any explicit allowance > 0 as authoritative instead of using max(explicit, INFINITY for minters).

harm.who: users interacting with minters (hub bids, bridge, positions) who hold a small stale allowance
harm.loses_what: availability: transactions revert until allowance is reset to 0
harm.magnitude: temporary denial of the intended no-approval flow

exploit_trace: 1. User approves the MintingHub for 1 wei (or a smaller amount than later needed).
2. User later calls bid() needing zchf.transferFrom(user, hub, X) with X > 1.
3. allowanceInternal returns 1 (explicit > 0), transferFrom reverts ERC20InsufficientAllowance even though the hub is a minter.

preconditions.text: user has a nonzero explicit allowance smaller than the amount for a minter or position spender

postconditions.text: call reverts until allowance reset to 0

postconditions_created: call reverts until allowance reset to 0
